title: Decision review: example
subtitle: Reusable review layout · Example content
intro: Review the practical scenario, choose an approach, and leave your reasoning. Nothing is preselected.
notice: These fictional questions demonstrate the layout. They are not pending decisions for your project.

items.title: How should reviewers receive the artifact?
items.decision: Choose how to package a review for another person.
items.problem: This is a fictional example for demonstrating the review interface. Media files must stay next to the HTML.
items.scenario: A reviewer receives the questions and two screenshots, then opens the review while offline.
items.recommendation: Share the complete directory as a ZIP when attachments are allowed. It keeps the HTML and media together.
items.question: Which delivery format fits the workflow?
checks: The recipient can open the HTML and see every image without a network connection.
Choices and comments remain after reloading the same page in the same browser.

options.title: Share a ZIP of the complete folder
options.detail: The recipient extracts the folder and opens review.html.
options.cost: The recipient must extract the archive before opening it.

steps: Package review.html, review.json, the manifest, and assets together.
Send the archive through the existing authorized sharing channel.
proposal.failure: If attachments are blocked, the review remains local until another sharing method is chosen.
proposal.scope: Packaging the artifact; external delivery still follows the user's instructions.

options.title: Use a shared folder
options.detail: Place the complete bundle in an existing shared directory.
options.cost: Reviewers need access to that directory and may need to download it for offline use.

steps: Copy the complete bundle into the agreed directory.
Give the reviewer the HTML location and tell them to keep the assets folder beside it.
proposal.failure: A reviewer without access cannot open the bundle until access is resolved.
proposal.scope: Using an existing shared destination; no new public hosting.

items.title: What feedback should the reviewer return?
items.decision: Choose the normal handoff format after the review.
items.problem: Readable feedback and resumable browser state serve different purposes.
items.scenario: The reviewer has selected one option and left a question on another. The author needs to act on both.
items.recommendation: Return Markdown for discussion and keep JSON as a backup. Send both when someone else needs to resume editing.
items.question: What should the handoff include?
checks: The Markdown export includes the selected option, comment, and unresolved question.
Importing the JSON into an unchanged review restores all choices and comments.

options.title: Return readable Markdown
options.detail: Send Export feedback output and keep a personal JSON backup.
options.cost: The recipient can read the feedback but cannot restore editable state from Markdown alone.

steps: Export feedback after reviewing the summary.
Download Backup JSON for personal recovery.
proposal.failure: If the editable state is lost, restore it from the saved JSON backup.
proposal.scope: A readable feedback handoff; no automatic implementation approval.

options.title: Return Markdown and JSON
options.detail: Send both exports so the recipient can read or resume the review.
options.cost: Two files must be kept together with the matching version of the review.

steps: Identify the review version when returning the two files.
proposal.failure: A backup from a changed review is rejected instead of applying choices to different proposals.
proposal.scope: Readable feedback plus resumable state for the exact reviewed content.
